newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Aide dismisses chance of Netanyahu indictment.
newsitem.headline: Aide dismisses chance of Netanyahu indictment.

text.p: An aide to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Thursday he did not believe the State Prosecutor would implement a police recommendation that Netanyahu be charged with fraud and breach of trust.

Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh, while admitting if charges were made they could result in Netanyahu's "dismissal", said the police recommendation was not well-enough founded "to change the course of history".

Naveh told Israel's army radio he was quoting from a police letter to the prosecutor regarding the recommendation: "We are aware of the problematics of presenting an indictment on an issue that is so complicated and sensitive based on one central witness who could be seized on and presented by the defence as untrustworthy and perhaps even an interested party."

Naveh then said: "And I want to ask, do you present an indictment against the prime minister in Israel, something that could in effect bring about the dismissal of the prime minister in Israel, pervert the wishes of the voters of only a year ago, change the course of the history of the State of Israel on a basis like this? My answer to this question is negative."

Police said on Wednesday Netanyahu should be charged with fraud and breach of trust in an influence-peddling scandal. They acknowledged the recommendation was based on the testimony of a single witness.
Israel's state prosecutor can choose to ignore the police recommendation to put Netanyahu on trial for his short-lived appointment of political crony Roni Bar-On as attorney general in January.
